studentEssentials.title: International Student Accommodation Guide
studentEssentials.summary: Comparing On-Campus Halls, Purpose-Built Student Accommodation (PBSA), and Private Shared Flats.
studentEssentials.details: On-campus dorms provide convenience and guaranteed bills included; PBSA (like Unite Students, Scape, Campus Living Villages) offer en-suite rooms and gyms; private shared flats (via portals like SpareRoom, WG-Gesucht, Flatmates) offer greater independence and lower costs.
checklists: Verify whether heating and Wi-Fi are included
Never transfer money to unverified private listings

studentEssentials.title: Living Costs & Monthly Budgeting
studentEssentials.summary: Realistic monthly breakdown for housing, groceries, utilities, transit, and mobile in major destination countries.
checklists: Budget for initial bond/deposit (usually 4-6 weeks rent)
Use student discount cards (UNiDAYS, Student Beans)
Cook at home to save up to 60% on food expenses

studentEssentials.title: Mobile Connectivity & International eSIMs
studentEssentials.summary: How to stay connected the moment your flight touches down without exorbitant roaming bills.
studentEssentials.details: Getting a physical SIM at foreign airport kiosks often costs 3x more. Setting up an international eSIM before departure allows immediate WhatsApp connectivity for parents upon landing.
checklists: Verify if your phone is carrier-unlocked and eSIM-compatible
Install the QR profile before departure in India
Activate data roaming on the eSIM profile upon landing

studentEssentials.title: Overseas Banking, Forex & Money Transfers
studentEssentials.summary: Opening digital student accounts (Revolut, Monzo, N26, Commonwealth Bank) and safe remittance.
studentEssentials.details: Carry a multi-currency Forex card loaded with initial funds (£1,000 / €1,000 / $1,500) for your first 2 weeks. Open a local student bank account using your university confirmation letter and passport.
checklists: Carry minimal cash (approx. 200-300 units of destination currency)
Keep Forex card separate from physical passport
Use authorized RBI-compliant remittance channels for tuition fees

studentEssentials.title: Pre-Departure Flight & Packing Checklist
studentEssentials.summary: Essential documents, prescription medications, attire, and adapters to pack in your hand luggage.
studentEssentials.details: Always keep your passport, visa grant letter, university CAS/I-20/LOA, original degree certificates, TB certificate, and prescription letters in your cabin bag. Never check in essential legal documents.

Original marksheets & transcripts in sealed envelope
Universal power adapter and power bank
30-day supply of personal medications with doctor prescription

faqs.question: Do you guarantee admission or visas?
faqs.answer: No. Athmanathan Study Abroad upholds complete transparency and ethical counselling: we never guarantee admissions, scholarships, or visa approvals. Final decisions are made solely by universities and immigration authorities. We guide you meticulously to maximize the quality and accuracy of your application.

faqs.question: Is IELTS mandatory for studying abroad?
faqs.answer: While many top universities in the UK, USA, Australia, and Canada prefer IELTS/PTE, several universities offer Medium of Instruction (MOI) waivers if your entire degree was conducted in English with high English marks in Class 12. We assess your profile to identify options with and without English testing.

faqs.question: Can I study abroad if I have a study gap after graduation?
faqs.answer: Yes. Universities and visa authorities accept study gaps provided they are justified with genuine documentation, such as employment letters, pay slips, bank statements, certifications, or medical records. We help you present your career timeline clearly.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to show for my student visa?
faqs.answer: Financial requirements vary strictly by country: UK requires 9 months of living expenses (~£9,207 outside London or £12,006 in London) held for 28 consecutive days; Germany requires a Blocked Account of ~€11,208; Canada requires a GIC of CAD $20,635; Australia requires proof of AUD 29,710 for one year. We provide exact guidance based on current official embassy criteria.

faqs.question: Why should I buy an eSIM before leaving India?
faqs.answer: An international eSIM lets you connect to local mobile networks the instant your flight touches down. You avoid expensive international roaming fees and can immediately call parents on WhatsApp and order an Uber from the airport without hunting for an airport SIM counter.

faqs.question: Can I bring my spouse or children while studying abroad?
faqs.answer: Rules have tightened across destinations: UK allows dependants only for postgraduate research programs (like PhD); Canada restricts open work permits for spouses primarily to Master/PhD and specific professional programs; Australia and Germany continue to have designated family reunion / dependant provisions under specific criteria. We review your family situation individually.

faqs.question: What is the relationship with Happy Journey Holidays?
faqs.answer: Happy Journey Holidays is our associated travel and support partner. They assist our students with competitive airfares, extra baggage allowances for international students, airport transit, and travel insurance. Both brands maintain separate operations and distinct service areas.

testimonials.quote: Athmanathan Study Abroad gave me completely honest advice. They never promised fake shortcuts; instead, they helped refine my SOP and financial documents so my visa arrived within 11 days. Highly recommend for Indian students!

My dream was to pursue healthcare in Australia. The guidance on IELTS preparation (got 7.5 overall) and clinical requirements was top tier. The team supported me right until I settled into my Melbourne accommodation.

Navigating APS certificates and German blocked accounts seemed daunting. The Athmanathan counsellors guided me through every step patiently. Studying in Germany tuition-free has transformed my career.
